Obfuscation part II: Diamond iO

Indistinguishability obfuscation is a cryptographic primitive that asks whether a program can be transformed into an equivalent program whose internal structure is hidden.

The Diamond iO line of work tries to make obfuscation constructions more concrete by reorganizing the building blocks and making the assumptions easier to inspect.

The post explains why this is still research, not a ready-to-deploy primitive, and why efficiency, assumptions, and verification remain the main constraints.
